raw_case_text:
A 29-year-old primigravida started with pain and mild heaviness in the both lower limbs distally associated with occasional pins and needles sensation in 35th week of pregnancy. Her symptoms were progressive. Over the next 10 days, the patient noticed knee buckling with frequent falls and difficulty in sitting and standing from supine position. At the end of 36th week, an emergency LSCS (lower segment caesarian section) was performed for decreased fetal heart rate. LSCS was uneventful and a healthy baby was born. Second post-partum day, the patient was discharged. On third post-partum day, the patient complained of weakness all the four limbs (in addition to persisting symptoms), more in lower limbs and was not able to maintain the erect posture. In this state, the patient was brought to our accident and emergency department. A detailed history was taken which revealed initiation of symptoms during third trimester of pregnancy without any preceding illness. Subsequent clinical examination revealed sinus tachycardia, fluctuating hypertension, power of 4/5 in upper limbs, 3/5 in lower limbs, hypotonia, areflexia (lower limbs), flexor plantar response, and mild involvement of all the modalities of sensation. A working diagnosis of GBS was made and all other investigations including nerve conduction studies, arterial blood gases, electrolytes, and later cerebrospinal fluid analysis were planned.
Arterial blood gas analysis showed pO2=89 mmHg, saturation = 94.6%, pCO2=42 mmHg, and pH = 7.39. Serum potassium was 4.1 meq/L, sodium 136 meq/L and bicarbonate 25 meq/L. Electrocardiography showed sinus tachycardia and routine blood chemistry was normal. Serological tests for campylobacter jejuni, EBV, cytomegalovirus, and mycoplasma pneumonae were negative. Electrophysiological studies revealed decreased amplitude of compound action potentials in median and common peronial nerves with decreased conduction velocity and abnormal F waves. After 7 days, lumbar puncture was performed and cerebrospinal fluid chemistry revealed raised protein of 7.8 g/L and normal cell count, confirming the diagnosis. The patient received treatment in the form of physiotherapy and close observation of symptoms and signs to which she rapidly responded with respect to power and sense of well-being over next 72 h, without the intervention of immunomodulating drugs. Sinus tachycardia and episodic hypertension was treated with atenolol. The patient was discharged after 2 weeks of hospital stay with power of 5/5 in upper limbs, 4+/5 in right lower limb, and 4/5 in left lower limb with persisting areflexia in lower limbs.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 29-year-old primigravida presented on postpartum day 3 with progressive four-limb weakness (worse in the lower extremities) and inability to stand upright.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: At 35 weeks of gestation, without any preceding infectious illness, the patient developed progressive distal lower-limb pain, mild heaviness, paresthesias ('pins and needles'), knee buckling, frequent falls, and difficulty rising from a supine or seated position. She underwent an emergency lower segment cesarean section (LSCS) at the end of week 36 for fetal bradycardia (delivering a healthy infant) and was discharged on postpartum day 2, but returned to the emergency department on postpartum day 3 with quadriparesis and inability to maintain an erect posture.
subjective.past_medical_history: Recent primigravid pregnancy delivered at 36 weeks' gestation via emergency cesarean section for fetal distress; no preceding infectious illness.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for distal lower extremity pain, heaviness, paresthesias, progressive lower-then-upper limb weakness, falls, and inability to stand.

objective.physical_examination: Sinus tachycardia, fluctuating hypertension, hypotonia, muscle power 4/5 in bilateral upper limbs and 3/5 in bilateral lower limbs, lower-limb areflexia, flexor plantar responses, and mild pan-modal sensory impairment.
objective.routine_investigations: ABG: pH 7.39, pO2 89 mmHg, pCO2 42 mmHg, SpO2 94.6%. Electrolytes and routine biochemistry normal (potassium 4.1 mEq/L, sodium 136 mEq/L, bicarbonate 25 mEq/L). ECG showed sinus tachycardia. Serological tests for Campylobacter jejuni, Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), cytomegalovirus (CMV), and Mycoplasma pneumoniae were all negative.
objective.advanced_workup: Nerve conduction studies demonstrated reduced compound muscle action potential (CMAP) amplitudes, slowed conduction velocities, and abnormal F-waves in the median and common peroneal nerves. Lumbar puncture performed 7 days after presentation showed albuminocytologic dissociation with elevated CSF protein (7.8 g/L) and a normal CSF cell count.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Definitive diagnosis of pregnancy/postpartum-associated Guillain-Barre syndrome (GBS) with autonomic dysfunction (confirmed by ascending areflexic quadriparesis, demyelinating/axonal features with abnormal F-waves on nerve conduction studies, and CSF albuminocytologic dissociation [protein 7.8 g/L, normal cells]; C. jejuni, CMV, EBV, and M. pneumoniae ruled out). Managed conservatively with close monitoring, physiotherapy, and oral atenolol for autonomic sinus tachycardia and episodic hypertension, achieving rapid spontaneous motor improvement within 72 hours (without IVIG or plasmapheresis) and hospital discharge at 2 weeks with 5/5 upper limb strength and 4+/5 right / 4/5 left lower limb strength.
